name: Udupi
headline: Near-perfect SSLC results; documented exits are mostly students absent from board papers.
summary: Udupi shares Dakshina Kannada's profile: 98.18% SSLC pass in 2026 (second in the state) after intensive slow-learner coaching. The only dropout-like signal in the sources is students who sit the whole secondary cycle and then skip board papers, 62 in language papers in 2026 and 122 in science papers in an earlier cycle. Early-secondary dropout is rarely reported.

reasons.detail: Students from several blocks failed to appear for language papers in 2026 and for science papers in an earlier cycle, a late exit that official pass rates hide.
Teachers are told to isolate weaker students and drill them with question banks after preparatory exams, which keeps Class 10 candidates in the system.

The Deputy Commissioner reported complaints of under-14s collecting fish at Malpe harbour despite earlier raids, and said officials should focus on school dropouts, who tend to end up in child labour.

Rescue operations at Malpe port found children working there, including 17 from Bellary and Koppal in October 2020 and three in a 2023 joint operation, suggesting inbound labour migration rather than local dropout.

The district education office identified 3,080 slow learners in Class 9 and prepared a passing package, with the district pass rate around 88 percent. Exam-related exit risk is implied but not stated.
117 students were absent on the first SSLC exam day across 58 centres out of about 13,700 enrolled in the district, a small share.

responses.text: Education officials mandate slow-learner coaching and question-bank drills after the preparatory exam.
The Deputy Commissioner asked for periodic surprise raids at Malpe harbour, stronger action against employers, and awareness among parents so under-14s are kept in school.
The district education office created a passing package for 3,080 identified Class 9 slow learners to raise the SSLC pass rate.
Joint child-protection rescues at Malpe port took working children into the child welfare committee system.

English-medium schooling is common here, but no source links it to retention or dropout.

gaps: No Class 8-10 dropout counts; most sources are SSLC-result coverage; the district's very low casefile dropout rate is unexplained. Article dates mostly unknown; several pages returned 403 or 404 so details rest on search excerpts. No UDISE+ figures, post-COVID trend, girls or child marriage evidence, or source explaining the low rate (reporting differences, migration out) found.
